payload.text: The testkit sweep-order fix for 3.2.9, assigned by vc at 10:32Z on vc's date -u on 2026-11-01 under hv's bug-fix word (vc decision 106). sweep_abandoned_fixtures took its live-pid snapshot before it listed /tmp (testkit/src/lib.rs:421-445), so a fixture whose process was born between the two was removed while its process lived. The fix lists the candidates first and takes the snapshot second, in one sweep body, sweep_abandoned_fixtures_around, through whose seam the new test a_fixture_planted_by_a_process_born_mid_sweep_survives_it plants a live child's fixture. vc approved the seam. It is banked at refs/bank/dc/testkit-sweep-order/fix-v1 (blob 6459397b30b4, patch-id 3e958d267455), stacked on fd4aced67 plus refs/bank/dc/testkit-race/fix-v1 (tree 4589b880e19b) in tmp/wt-dc-sweeporder, with its mutant at refs/bank/dc/testkit-sweep-order/red-v1 (patch-id f70636f75203) and its issue draft at refs/bank/dc/testkit-sweep-order/issue.title.txt and issue.body-v2.md (issue.body.md is the earlier draft). dc's run is desk ask 01M6BB981X1E5KDPVY3E7CBWK6, after the race proof in devbin-vc's order: the test 20 times red on the mutant and 20 times green on the fix, then the whole workspace suite, workspace clippy and fmt, since testkit's lib runs at every crate's test start. vc's judge follows under an exclusive grant, since until both fixes land an old-testkit sweeper elsewhere on the box can still take the test's fixture. vc records both testkit issues after the push and dc claims them then; both land after the push on vc's word. The race proof's storm also reproduced the defect without the seam: in a 2s capture after it, all 7 sibling failures of 160 runs were at :106, a LIVE fixture was deleted, which issue.body-v2.md records as observed evidence, and dc's run adds that sibling storm on the mutant and the fix, on vc's yes. No CHANGELOG entry, since testkit is unshipped.
